scholarships.name: Black Hills State University S-STEM Scholarships
scholarships.criteria:
Participants must pursue a major in Biology, Chemistry, Physical Science, Environmental Physical Science, or Mathematics.
Students must also have demonstrated financial need (as indicated on the Free Application for Federal Student Aid, or FAFSA) and have a strong academic record.
Students selected for the S-STEM Scholars Program may receive up to $10,000 in annual scholarship, which is renewable for up to four years.
These scholarship dollars can be stacked on top of any other financial aid you receive from Black Hills State University. Applicants must be citizens or nationals of the United States.

Applicants who have completed dual-credit undergraduate courses during high school are eligible and encouraged to apply.
TO APPLY
Apply for admission to Black Hills State University
Submit the S-STEM Scholarship application, including:
Reference Contact Information:
Provide contact information (first and last name, email address) for a science or math teacher who knows you well and is willing to write a letter of recommendation.
Ask that teacher to provide their assessment of you at this link BHSU.edu/S-Stem Recommender Form
A response of 350 words (maximum) to the following:
What interests you about science and math and how do you think the additional support offered by the S-STEM Scholars Program will help you succeed in your STEM career?
Submit the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA), which you can access on the FAFSA site Studentaid.gov/apply-for-aid/FAFSA

scholarships.name: Black American Engineering Scholarship
scholarships.criteria: This scholarship is provided by The Helping Project Corp and is dedicated to creating diversity in the field of engineering and further dismantling institutional racism toward Black Americans in STEM careers. The scholarship provides up to $10,000 per year ($5,000 per semester) of funding and can be applied for up to four years. It is aimed at providing a pathway to achievement for Black Americans pursuing careers in civil, mechanical, electrical, and chemical engineering. Selected candidates receive substantial assistance designed to close the financial gap left after the Pell Grant is used for tuition. The funds can be used for school expenses like tuition, books, fees, and room and board. Scholarship recipients also participate in a mentorship program designed to support their professional success​1​. To apply, applicants must be a Black American incoming college freshman/current high school senior or a student transferring from a two-year program into a four-year program. They must be eligible for Federal Pell Grant funding and able to show proven financial need. They must also be a U.S. citizen, national, or permanent resident in good academic standing who is enrolling in an accredited, not-for-profit four-year institution. The degree pursued must be in civil, electrical, mechanical, or chemical engineering, including any subfield of those disciplines​1​.

scholarships.name: The Hagan Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
The Hagan Scholarship is a nationwide need-based merit scholarship, providing recipients with the opportunity to graduate college debt-free. 1. Must be a U.S. Citizen.
2. Must attend a traditional public high school located in the U.S. that is governed by a school district.
3. Must have achieved a 3.50 Cumulative Grade Point Average.
4. Must enroll at an Eligible Four-Year College or University the first semester following high school graduation.
5. Must maintain a four year or less graduation schedule in college.
6. Must work 240 hours from January 1, 2024 until commencement of the 2024 fall semester in college. Work can be performed at recipient discretion. Work must be regularly scheduled employment performed under supervision for compensation.
7. Applicant’s Adjusted Gross Household Income reported for 2022 Federal Income Tax Purposes must not have exceeded $85,000. “Household Income” is defined as the total income received by all members of a household living under the same roof.
8. Finalists will be notified in February 2024. Finalists must provide a copy of their FAFSA SAR showing their EFC.
9. Must apply for Federal and State grants if eligible.
10. Must not have a felony conviction.

The intended recipient is a high-achieving goal-driven student having substantial financial need.
scholarships.amount: The scholarship provides up to $7.500 each semester for up to eight consecutive semesters.

scholarships.name: Stop Hunger Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Stephen J. Brady Stop Hunger Scholarships are open to students ages 5-25 (Kindergarten through graduate school) enrolled in an accredited educational institution in the United States.
Applicants must have demonstrated on-going commitment to their community by performing unpaid volunteer services impacting hunger in the United States at least within the last 12 months. Added consideration is given to students working to fight childhood hunger.

All applicants must be citizens or permanent residents of the United States who reside in the contiguous United States, Alaska, and Hawaii only.

Volunteer services must be helping non-family members.

Applicants must obtain a Community Service Recommendation / Volunteer Service Verification as part of the application process.

Recommenders must be at least 21 years of age, may NOT be your parent, guardian or family member.

Employees of Sodexo are not eligible to apply for the Stephen J. Brady Stop Hunger Scholarships; but they may refer family members who are not employees of Sodexo.

Previous national Stephen J. Brady Stop Hunger Scholarships recipients are not eligible to apply.

Previous Stop Hunger Regional Honorees are eligible to apply.

scholarships.name: Day County Coyote Hunt Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:

Applicants must be 19 years of age or younger. You must be a graduating senior from an accredited high school during the year of application. This scholarship may also be granted to a family member of a SD National Guard soldier who is physically challenged as determined by the American Disabilities Act passed on July 25, 1990.
Scholarships must be used in one of the following types of accredited post-high school institutions: College, University or Vocational Technical School. Scholarships will be paid directly to the school.
Applicant must ascertain their own eligibility to receive such a scholarship according to the eligibility rules of the institution they will be attending. If, for any reason, the original recipient is unable to attend college in the year of application, the awarded scholarship monies may be held for an additional year, after which time, it may be re-deposited in the scholarship fund.

scholarships.criteria: The USA Softball of South Dakota Program has been established to award scholarships to those who have participated in USA Softball of South Dakota & desire to further their education. These participants must have participated in the USA Softball of South Dakota sanctioned programs for at least 3 years as a player, coach, umpire, USA Softball of South Dakota official, or in a official capacity of a USA Softball of South Dakota sanctioned team or league. Applicants must be 19 years of age or younger. You must be a graduating senior from an accredited high school during the year of application. This scholarship may also be granted to a family member of USA Softball of South Dakota memeber who is physically challenged as determined by the American Disabilities Act passed on July 25th, 1990.

scholarships.name: Adam Bauer Scholarship
scholarships.criteria: An eligible senior candidate will have participated in BV athletics during his/her high school career and completed the entire season. Although not the only criteria, special attention will be given to the athlete who has participted in two or three sports in all four years of high school. GPA will be reviewed but will not be the biggest factor. Eligible candidates must be attending a post-secondary school in the fall following graduation. If the application will not open for you, try clicking on the open with google sheets when prompted. If that doesn't work, e-mail Kara.Likness@k12.sd.us and request an email attached copy. Applications can be submitted electronically to Merry.Miller@k12.sd.us or via mail to the Business Office (300 S. Splitrock Blvd) in care of Merry Miller.

scholarships.name: Fuji Film & Urban Outfitters Scholarhsips
scholarships.criteria:
This contest is open only to legal residents of United States and the District of Columbia. Entrant must be sixteen (16) years of age or older at the time of application. Applicants must attend or plan to attend a two-year or four-year college, university or vocational/technical school.Complete the application, including essay questions by October 16th.
You will be notified by November 8th if you are one of the one hundred (100) semi-finalists.
Semi-finalists will be asked to create a 1 (one) minute video on a specific topic chosen by Urban Outfitters + Fujifilm. Videos must be submitted by November 24th.
One grand prize winner will receive $10,000 and two second prize winners will receive $5,000 each. Winners will be notified on or around December 28th.
scholarships.amount: One award of $10,000 & two awards of $5,000

scholarships.name: Geneva Rock Scholarship
scholarships.criteria: To be eligible, applicants must be currently enrolled in an accredited university, college, trade or vocational school. Scholarship applicants must be in pursuit of construction-related careers including, but not limited to: Construction management, civil engineering, business, and commercial/professional sales. Students involved in trades such as welding, diesel tech, heavy equipment operations and building tech are also welcome to apply. High school seniors are eligible to apply, but must be enrolled in one of the previously mentioned institutions. All applicants must have received, (or be in the process of attaining), their high school diploma or GED. All applicants must be U.S. citizens, or be a legal permanent resident with work eligibility status.

scholarships.name: Bryan Cameron Education Foundation
James H. Jenssen Scholarship Application
scholarships.criteria: To be eligible for the scholarship you must meet all of the following criteria: -be a resident of the state of SD and a high school senior OR be a resident of the state of SD and enrolled in an engineering program at South Dakota School of Mines or South Dakota State University for the upcoming academic year -Be a US citizen . -Have a parent, grandparent, sibling, uncle aunt or cousin employed a minimum of 3 years (or retired) with the South Dakota Deparment of Transportation. -Have a current high school GPA of 3.0 (based on 4.0 grading system) or higher OR a minimum of a 3.0 GPA at School of Mines or SDSU if currently attending. -Demonstrate ability to become an asset to the engineering field. -Must not be a relative of James H. Jenssen.

scholarships.name: Private Frontier Scholarship Essay Contest
scholarships.criteria: students ages 12-18. Essay of 500-1000 words on the topic: Certain endeavors were always considered a job for government, but entrepreneurs have changed that. Consider space exploration. Elon Musk's SpaceX recently sent two astronauts into space for two months. But it's not just up in space that entrepreneurs are making changes. Down here on Earth, entrepreneurs are forcing us to reconsider what private enterprise might do better than government does. Education and the Postal Service are two other examples of numerous government-run operations that might face similar challenges from private enterprise. Is this the future? Is society better served with greater involvement from entrepreneurs? If so, who pays and who profits?

scholarships.name: National Cyber Scholarship Competition
scholarships.criteria: This NCS Competition is a new type of CTF that has challenges for every level. Students can qualify for the National Cyber Scholarship Competition through CyberStart America, beginning on October 30, 2020, or through alternative entry routes include the Spring picoCTF competition and the CyberPatriot program. Qualified students will compete nationally to win one of three tiers of award, with the highest scorers being awarded college scholarships to use at the school of their choice to pursue further study related to cybersecurity. This CTF competition will allow students to rank highly by completing challenges across a range of disciplines, or to focus their efforts on a particular area, such as defensive hacking.

scholarships.name: Endeavor Design Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
The Endeavour Design Scholarship is offered in support of creating racial equity in the fields of Fashion/Footwear, Industrial, and Graphic Design.

Requirements:

Scholarship reserved for Black High School students, US residents only.
Must be a High School Senior/Student or Returning Freshman, 2nd Semester College Student who plans to enroll in a full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college
Pursuing a design-related degree; majors include: Fashion Design, Footwear Design, Industrial Design, Graphic Design, or related fields.
To apply, submit 5-7 photos of your portfolio. Write a brief statement about what design means to you and how a career in design would be transformational for you.

scholarships.name: Bank of American Student Leaders Program
scholarships.criteria:
Currently be a junior or senior in high school
Live in one of the eligible markets listed
Be able to participate in an 8‐week paid internship at a local nonprofit/charitable organization and work 35 hours a week*
Be legally authorized to work in the US without sponsorship through the end of September 2022
Be able to participate in a week‐long Student Leadership Summit in Washington, DC (July 25-30, 2022) (All expenses paid as part of Student Leaders. This week will be part of your 8‐ week experience.) *
Be a student in good standing at your school
Please note: Bank of America employees or members of their immediate family (e.g., children, siblings, grandchildren, nieces, nephews, etc.) are NOT eligible to apply.

scholarships.name: Youth Citizenship and Americanism Scholarship American Legion High School Award
scholarships.criteria: Legion Post 318 requests the candidates write a 500-1,000 word essay to inform the selection board of the qualities they possess as young citizens. In the essay, they are asked to choose three of the qualities the Legion seeks to develop in our citizens (courage, honor, leadership, patriotism, scholarship and service) and explain how those three qualities have molded their lives. Additionally, a description of the candidate's volunteerism should be included. The candidates may include: one letter of recommendation, and /or one reference document in your essay. The candidates need to present the essay and reference material together. The letter of recommendation needs to be addressed: To Whom It May Concern.
scholarships.amount: 1 senior boy and 1 senior girl - $250 each

scholarships.name: APIA Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
APIA SCHOLARS MINIMUM ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA :
Be of Asian and/or Pacific Islander ethnicity as defined by the U.S. Census
Be a citizen, national, or legal permanent resident of the United States. Citizens of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Federated States of Micronesia and the Republic of Palau are also eligible to apply
Be enrolling as an undergraduate student in a U.S. accredited college or university in the Fall of 2024.
Have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 on a 4.0 scale (unweighted) or have earned a GED
Must apply for federal financial aid for the 2023-2024 academic year using the Free Application for the Federal Student Aid (FASFA) by early April 2024
Submit one letter of recommendation online

scholarships.name: Fred M. Young Sr./SAE Engineering Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
U.S. Resident
Incoming Freshman
Minimum unweighted 3.75 grade point average
Pursue an engineering or related science degree through a U.S. ABET accredited program with an interest in mobility (Automotive, Ground or Air)
Provide two (2) Letters of Recommendation - one (1) that focuses on academics and one (1) that speaks to your involvement in extra-curricular activities or employment
Serve in a leadership role inside or outside of school and be able to outline how your leadership skills were developed, the size of the team(s) led and how your personal leadership skills will benefit you in your future career.
Must be able to detail how 2 traits of an engineer (from listed provided) apply to them.

scholarships.name: The Lawrence Novotny Scholarship Essay Competition
scholarships.criteria:
The Lawrence Novotny Scholarship Essay Competition has chosen to provide scholarships to high school seniors who are heading to ANY college, university, technical school, trade school etc., as well as current college, university, technical school, trade school etc. Students who are post high school can be enrolled in any field of study, but they must be completing their secondary education in South Dakota.
Applicants will have a packet of information submitted which will also include a completed essay on the following topic:
In the wake of Anti-2SLGBTQ+ legislation that has swept America in the past couple of years, why should we be able to talk about these issues in an educational context?
scholarships.amount: (1) $250 for a graduating high school senior student

scholarships.name: South Dakota Fire SERVICE Scholarship Program
scholarships.criteria: A son or daughter of any member (living, deceased or retired) of a fire department in South Dakota or an active member of a junior fire department in South Dakota. A high school senior or student entering their first semester of college. The applicatn must be a sponsored by a fire department that has 100% membership in the SD Firefighters Association for the current year. The applicant may also be sponsored by a member of the SD Firefighters Auxiliary, a local fire department auxiliary or a member of the Dear Old Timers. The scholarship may be used at any college or post-secondary institution. Preference will be given to those who are obtaining a fire science or emergency service degree.

scholarships.name: DAR Good Citizens Program and Scholarship Contest
scholarships.criteria: Open to one senior class student. Student must be dependable(which includes truthfulness, loyalty, and punctuality); service(cooperation, courtesy, and consideration of others); leadership(personality, self-control, and ability to assume responsibility); and patriotism(includes unselfish interest in family, school, community and nation) to an outstanding degree. There are 2 parts to this scholarship contest. Part 1 includes describing how you have tried to manifest the qulities of a good citizen. Part 2 includes a timed essay to be administered under the supervision of a faculty member. Must be completed at one sitting, within a two-hour time limit, and without assistance of references.

scholarships.name: ROTC Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
REQUIREMENTS
Be a U.S. citizen
Be between the ages of 17 and 26
Have a high school GPA of at least 2.50
Have a high school diploma or equivalent
Score a minimum of 1000 on the SAT (math/verbal) or 19 on the ACT (excluding the required writing test scores)
Meet physical standards
Agree to accept a commission and serve in the Army on Active Duty or in a Reserve Component (Army Reserve or Army National Guard)
YOUR COMMITMENT
An eight-year service commitment with the Army.
Serve full time in the Army for four years and four years with the Individual Ready Reserve (IRR).
Selected Cadets may choose to serve part time in the Army Reserve or Army National Guard while pursuing a civilian career

scholarships.name: Flavorful Futures Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Applications must meet ALL the following criteria:

Must be a U.S. citizen or permanent legal resident of the United States.
Must be a high school senior graduating.
Must have a cumulative high school grade point average (GPA) of at least 2.5 on a 4 point scale (high school/home schooled seniors).
Must enroll for Fall as a freshman or 1st year student in part-time or full-time study at a 2-year, 4-year, college, university, trade or vocational school. The school must be an accredited U.S. institution, and listed on the official website for the U.S. Department of Education.
Must not be a relative or dependent child of an employee of Talking Rain or any of its retail customers.

scholarships.name: South Dakota Nursery and Lanscape Association Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
SDNLA is proud to offer a $500.00 scholarship to a South Dakota High School student planning to major in a horticulture related field and to encourage the study and entering of the work place of Horticulture, Floriculture, Plant Pathology, Landscape Design, Turf Management and other allied subjects that pertain to the Green Industry.

ELIGIBILITY
Available to any South Dakota High School Student who will be graduating in the spring.
Scholarship awards will be based on scholastic record, as well as the student’s ability and sincerity in pursuing employment in the Green Industry.
The SDNLA scholarship is awarded once per year. Students may only receive the scholarship one time.

scholarships.name: Bridging the Dream Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Requirements: enrolled as a high school senior;
plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university
or vocational-technical school within one year of high school graduation; are able to
demonstrate financial need by being Pell Grant-eligible, are a diverse candidate “Diversity”
shall include, but not limited to: gender; disability; race; ethnicity, and being from an underserved
community), are able to demonstrate leadership abilities, demonstrate good moral character
in all aspects of his/her life, including personal, professional, educational, in his/her community, and
online presence. See website for official details.

scholarships.name: FFA Scholarship Opportunities - Multiple Scholarships available to FFA and Non-Members
scholarships.criteria:
Each scholarship has specific criteria that are defined by the sponsor when the scholarship is established. Please read the
scholarship description in the Scholarship Catalog to see if you qualify. Criteria that apply to all scholarships are listed below.
ALL scholarship applicants must:
 Be less than 23 years of age at time of application (February 1)
 Be current FFA members unless otherwise stated
 Be U.S. citizen or permanent resident
 Plan to attend post-secondary school in the U.S.
 Be a high school senior or currently enrolled in college
 Be a full-time student
o Actively attending classes
o Minimum 12 credit hours if enrolled in a post-secondary institution

scholarships.name: SDATAT Scholarship Program
scholarships.criteria:
Applicant must reside in South Dakota, are currently attending a South Dakota public, private,
parochial high school or a home school program, and lives in a town or township that is a current member of
SDATAT. (A membership list is available on the sdtownships.com website) or contact your local town/
township board. Graduates of the class of 2021 are eligible to apply for the scholarship. The student must use
the scholarship for a college, university, or vocational school which has a physical presence in South Dakota.
Applicants must complete an application form and submit it along with their essay on this year’s topic which can be found on the website.

scholarships.name: AFC Visionary Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Applicant must be currently enrolled as a High School Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, or Senior and, must be a United States citizen or eligible non-citizen. Relatives of the American College Foundation Staff are not eligible to apply. Financial need is NOT considered; all income levels are encouraged to apply. All applications for the American College Foundation's Visionary Scholarship Program will consist of:

-A completed American College Foundation Visionary Scholarship Application
-A copy of the student's most recent unofficial high school transcript
-A 500-word, typed, double-spaced essay on "Why College is Important to Me"
For Us college tuition only

scholarships.name: Levo Credit Union Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Eligibility:
Entrants must be a member of Sioux Falls Federal Credit Union in good standing, or meet the eligibility criteria and become a
member prior to submitting the entry form. Sioux Falls Federal Credit Union employees, volunteer officials, affiliates and their
relatives are ineligible. The applicant must show proof of enrollment before scholarship funds will be disbursed.
Submission Requirements
Each entry must include the following documents:
• Completed and signed application form.
• Letter of recommendation from an unrelated person who is familiar with the applicant’s community.
• Personal video or essay on your community service activities.

scholarships.name: HonorsGradU Scholarship: Design A Better Future
scholarships.criteria: Design and work on a community improvement project, using the website checklist as a guide. Applicants must be graduating high school seniors planning on attending an accredited college or university in the US. Additionally, students must have met all of the requirements described on the website. Students don’t have to have a minimum GPA to apply. In fact, we don’t even look at the GPA. All we look at is the work pertaining to the student’s project. This is because we know that grades do not always reflect a student’s potential or ability to contribute to society. This scholarship is open to all students, of all backgrounds and academic standings.
scholarships.deadline: OPTIONAL DEADLINES IN THE FALL TO HELP WITH PROJECT. See website for details. FINAL SUBMISSION DUE: 05/28/2022

scholarships.name: Scholarships for Undocu Students
scholarships.criteria: Hispanic students who are beginning or continuing their studies at higher educational institution and demonstrate leadership in extra-curricular activities, a commitment to volunteer service in the community and financial need; be an incoming or continuing full-time undergraduate student full-time; have a 3.0 GPA; be a U.S. Citizen, Permanent Legal Resident, Undocumented, DACA, CA Dreamer or Eligible Non-Citizen (as defined by FAFSA); and, must be a resident and attending a college in Arizona or California’s Central Valley (see website for more details). For more information or to apply, please visit the scholarship provider's website.

scholarships.name: South Dakota Elks Association Career & Technical Ed. Scholarship
scholarships.criteria: Applicatns must be enrolled or planning to enroll in an accredited post-secondary career and technical education program which teminates with completion of that program. Applicants shall have no immediate or long range plans to pursue a baccalaureate degree program. A 350-500 typed word essay about the student. This should include a description of the applicant, the applican'ts financial needs, the applican'ts involvement in extracurricular and community activities and a summary of the applican'ts intended career plans and goals. Explain the course of study or other activities taken to prepare for the student's anticipated career.

scholarships.name: Path to Success Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Eligibility

The scholarship is open to any high school senior, college student, or graduate student who is a legal resident of the United States and living in the U.S. The student also must be enrolled in a two – five year post-secondary institution for the Spring 2023 semester.
Employees of Jan Dils Attorneys at Law, their immediate families (parent, child, sibling, and spouse), as well as those living in the same households of such individuals (whether related or not), are not eligible to participate in the competition.
Candidates for this scholarship should have a minimum GPA of 3.0 or higher and be in good academic standing.

scholarships.name: INKAS Rising Star Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Be currently enrolled or intending to enroll (i.e., as of January 2023) as a full-time student in Business or Engineering areas of study at an accredited university in Canada or U.S.; and to support the application with appropriate documentation, including but not limited to: school transcripts (unofficial), invitation or acceptance letter from the institution.
Maintain a minimum 75% average or equal GPA from the most recent term/semester
Be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident of Canada, U.S. citizen or Green Card holder or student visa holder or study permit holder and be able to support it with a clear and legible photocopy.

scholarships.name: Spirit Of Giving Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
High school seniors and current college students planning to attend college or another form of post-secondary education for the full school year following the submission period are eligible to apply. Eligible institutions include but are not limited to four-year universities, community colleges, institutes of technology and accredited credential or certificate programs.

Applicants must meet all of the following criteria:

Planning to attend school in the following school year at an institution within the US.
Not an employee or family member of Wine Country Gift Baskets or Houdini Inc.
Not a previous winner of this scholarship.

scholarships.name: Navajo Nations Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Candidates for the Brown and Caldwell Navajo Nations Scholarship Program must be:

A United States citizen or permanent resident.
A full-time student enrolled at an accredited two-year junior or four-year undergraduate college, or a senior in high school with a letter of acceptance from the college or university to be attended.
Have or intend to declare a major in civil, chemical, mechanical, electrical or environmental engineering or one of the environmental sciences (e.g. geology, hydrogeology, ecology).
Cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale (or equivalent on a 5.0 scale).
An enrolled member of the Navajo Nation

scholarships.name: Horatio Alger National Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Be enrolled full time as a high school junior in the United States
Exhibit a strong commitment to pursue and complete a bachelor’s degree at an accredited non-profit public or private institution in the United States (students may start their studies at a two-year institution and then transfer to a four-year institution)
Demonstrate critical financial need ($55,000 or lower adjusted gross family income is required)
Be involved in co-curricular and community service activities
Display integrity and perseverance in overcoming adversity
Maintain a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 2.0; and
Be a United States citize

scholarships.name: Unity Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Unity Lodge #130 AF & AM located in Sioux Falls, SD will award scholarships to qualified applicants who are residents of South Dakota or are direct descendants of a Unity Lodge #130 member. These scholarships will be used to attend a post-secondary educational institution (college, university, technical school, etc.) located in South Dakota.

Successful candidates will demonstrate financial need, scholastic ability, and community involvement. Preference will be given to those having a connection, by blood or marriage, to a member of the Masonic fraternity, living or deceased; however, all are encouraged to apply.

scholarships.name: Hy-Vee/Sanford Legends Scholarship
scholarships.criteria: Qualifications: 1. Be a graduating senior as defined by your school in spring of 2022 2. Reside in or around the areas outlined in the map on the application 3. Commit to continue their education at a 2-year or 4-year College or University in the fall directly after graduation 4. Have a high school cumulative GPA of 2.5 or higher 5. Have participated or contributed to their high athletic program in a significant way 6. Display character and values that make them a positive role model within their respective community 7. *Be nominated by a school official (principal, athletic director, coach, teacher)
scholarships.link: Have not receive update scholarship information

scholarships.name: Dr Eugene Kramer Scholarship for Future Doctors of America
scholarships.criteria:
In order to apply, be a current undergraduate student at a university in the United States or a High School student that plans to attend university. The scholarship is geared towards students who plan to attend medical school in the future.

The winner of the scholarship will be selected by an essay competition. A single winner will be chosen based on a creative essay of less than 1000 words answering the following:

“Being a doctor comes with great responsibility. When you become a doctor, name something that you will you do that goes over and above the call of duty to give back to the world.”

scholarships.name: DAR National Society Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Applicants must be citizens of the United States.
Applicants must attend or plan to attend an accredited college or university in the United States.
All multi-year scholarships, typically renewable up to four years, must be for consecutive years of attendance.
Awards are based on academic excellence, commitment to the field of study, and/or financial need, or other restrictions on specific scholarships.
Awards are placed on deposit with the recipient’s college or university and any unused portion shall be returned to the DAR.
Applicants are only eligible to receive one scholarship from the DAR

scholarships.name: Unigo: Make Me Laugh Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Applicants must:

Must be 14 years of age or older at time of application.| Must be a legal U.S. resident.| Must be a resident of one of the 50 United States or the District of Columbia.| This award is for U.S. students.

Submit an online written response to the question:

"OMG... finding and applying for scholarships is serious business, but it's time to lighten things up a little. We don't want to know why you deserve $1,500 or how great your grades are, we simply want to LOL. Describe an incident in your life, funny or embarrassing (fact or fiction), and make us laugh!" (250 words or less)

scholarships.name: BBB Student of Integrity Award Scholarships
scholarships.criteria: Three high school seniors from South Dakota will each be granted $2,000 college scholarships. These awards are not based on ethnicity, need or grade point average, but recognize students who exemplify ethical behavior and personal integrity, and who demonstrate humility, courage, compassion and respect for their peers, teachers and community — values of the BBB. This year the application and recommendations are all submitted electronically. Applicants no longer mail their packet to a BBB office. It is important that students read the Application Guide before they fill out the application.

scholarships.name: Pierce Butler Scholarship
scholarships.criteria: The Minnesota Beta Chapter of Phi Kappa Psi recognizes excellence in the classroom, in leadership, and in the community for incoming freshmen men to the University of Minnesota. This scholarship is designed to promote academic excellence among a new generation of Golden Gophers while stewarding a positive campus atmosphere. By applying for the Pierce Butler Scholarship, applicants are under no obligation to join or otherwise become affiliated with the Phi Kappa Psi fraternity. Recipients of the scholarship historically have been chosen based on merit in academics and/or in the community.

scholarships.name: Honors Graduation: Build A Better Future Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Eligibility Criteria:
To be eligible for the scholarship, applicants must be graduating high school seniors planning on attending an accredited college or university in the United States of America. Additionally, students must have met all of the requirements described on this website (http://honorsgradu.com/). Employees of Honors Graduation and their families are not eligible to participate. Submissions must be received before the deadlines in order to qualify for the scholarship program. Mailed applications must be postmarked by that deadline. There are no citizenship requirements.

scholarships.name: Barbara Lotze Scholarship for Future Teachers
scholarships.criteria:
Eligibility:
Applicants must declare their intent to prepare for, and engage in, a career in physics teaching at the high school level and must, at the time the scholarship funds are received by the student, be:
A) An undergraduate student enrolled in an accredited two-year college, four-year college or a university; or a high school senior accepted for such enrollment.
B) Pursuing, or planning to pursue, a course of study leading toward a career in physics teaching in the high schools.
C) Showing promise of success in their studies, and
D) A citizen of the United States of America.

scholarships.name: Patriots of the American Revolution High School Essay Contest
scholarships.criteria:
This contest is open to students in public, private, and parochial schools, and registered home-study programs, in grades 9-12. Essays from students from all grades will be judged together, with one winning essay chosen at each level. Participating DAR chapters will select one essay as the chapter winner, to be sent on to the State level; the State will select one essay winner to present the state for judging a the Division level, and each Division level will also have one winner which will be sent on to the National contest. *See Ms. Likness with quesitons.
US school awards only

scholarships.name: AbbVie Cystic Fibrosis Scholarship
scholarships.criteria: Applicants must be United States citizens or a legal and permanent residents of the United States who have been diagnosed with CF by a physician and are enrolled in or awaiting acceptance from an accredited institution (i.e., college, university, or trade/vocational school) for an educational program during the upcoming academic year. Employees of AbbVie and their immediate family members are not eligible to apply. Healthcare providers and their immediate family members are not eligible to apply. For more information or to apply, please visit the scholarship provider's website.

scholarships.name: Sanford Future Health Professional Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
This scholarship can only be awarded to BVHS seniors attending colleges or universities in SD, ND, or MN. Both 2 and 4-year schools are acceptable.

- Students must be pursuing a future career in healthcare.

- Preference may be given to members of the healthcare-related school group, HOSA.

- Preference may be given to applicants with prior healthcare-related experience. Applicants must get a BVHS staff member to fill out and turn in a sponsor from on behalf of them. Forms can be printed from the application link or a printed copy can be picked up in the high school office.

scholarships.name: Ascent $1,000 Monthly Community Champions Scholarship Giveaway
scholarships.criteria: Eligibility. The Promotion is open only to: students that are (i) enrolled in a degree program at least half-time, or technical skills training program (for example, a coding bootcamp) and (ii) legal residents of one of the fifty United States or the District of Columbia or DACA status student, age 18 or older. Employees or agents of Sponsor or its parent or affiliate companies or suppliers, as well as the immediate family (spouse, parents, siblings and children) and household members of each such employee or agent, are not eligible. Legal entities are not eligible to enter

scholarships.name: Heisman High School Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Criteria For Application:
Senior students.
Students who have at least a weighted “B” grade average (3.0 GPA) during grades 9, 10, and 11.
Students who participate in at least one of 47 Heisman High School Scholarship recognized sports (see website) recognized by the International Olympic Committee or the National Federation of State High School Associations.
Students who have participated in volunteer service, community involvement or leadership within his/her school or community.
Students who are a resident of one of the 50 United States or the District of Columbia (D.C.).

scholarships.name: MGMA Western Section Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Scholarship applicants are required to be a member of MGMA.

Applicants must be enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate degree program relevant to medical practice management, including public health, business administration, healthcare administration and other related areas.

To be eligible to receive a scholarship, students must be enrolled in a degree program for the coming academic year at a university located within the United States.

Must reside in Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Utah, Washington or Wyoming

scholarships.name: Foot Locker Scholar Athletes
scholarships.criteria:
In order to be eligible for the Foot Locker Scholar Athletes program, the applicant must:
Be entering college in the fall as a Freshman at a four-year school for an undergraduate degree.
Be currently involved in high school sports, intramural sports, or community based sports.
Have a minimum GPA of 3.0.
Be a U.S. citizen or permanent legal resident (you will be asked to prove citizenship and age if you win).
Not be an employee, officer or director of Foot Locker, Inc., or any of its subsidiaries, or a member of the immediate family of such an employee, officer or director.

scholarships.name: Energy Pathway Scholarship: Tech, Trade & Community College
scholarships.criteria:

Past scholarship winners are ineligible to apply for the program. Applications consist of a questionnaire and essay. The following scholarship types will be awarded under the program as stated below:

$2,000 per student for a Utah technical college or community college scholarship

scholarships.name: Voyage Federal Credit Union Scholarships
scholarships.criteria: Available to full-time students who enroll in an accredited college, university, trade or technical school for the 2018-2019 school year. Voyage Federal Credit Union pays one payment in the fall to the college, university or school after applicatn's acceptance in that institution. Applications become the property of Voyage Federal Credit Union. All applicants must: be a graduating high school senior, have a minimum 2.5 cumulative GPA, be a primary Voyage FCU member in good standing, not be a Voyage FCU employee, director or committee member or an immediate family member.

scholarships.name: Equality South Dakota’s Audacity Award
scholarships.criteria: Equality South Dakota’s Audacity Award is a scholarship for 2SLGBTQ+ and allied students who have been engaging in community service and/or activism work that seeks to better the lives of 2SLGBTQ+ people in South Dakota. This award is available to high school seniors who are heading to ANY college, university, technical school, trade school etc., as well as current college, university, technical school, trade school etc. Students who are post high school can be enrolled in any field of study, but they must be completing their secondary education in South Dakota
scholarships.amount: (1) $250 for a graduating high school senior student

scholarships.name: South Dakota Telecommunications Association Scholarship
scholarships.criteria: Qualifying Students: Have a high school diploma or GED equivalent; Are accepted into or attending a multi-year program degree at any accredited techcical college or accredited post-secondary higher education institution in South Dakota for fall semseter; Are majoring in a degree/program or field of study that is useful in the telecommunications or broadband industry or which signficantly relies on the use of broadband services and related technologies; and a customer/member or have a parent or legal guardian that is a customer/member of a SDTA member company.

scholarships.name: Southeast Area Principals Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
• All students applying to receive this scholarship award are required to fully complete all sections of this application packet. All questions must be answered and essay completed.

•Discuss your future plans (school / career) and how your education prepared you for your next step.
•Applicant’s School Principal must be an active member of the Southeast Area Principals Group.
•$500 Scholarship will payable after successful completion of 1 semester at a Post-Secondary Institution.

scholarships.name: Cyber America
scholarships.criteria:
CyberStart America gives students in 9th-12th grade free access to the world-renowned CyberStart game.

Tackle four unique bases, each focusing on both offensive and defensive cybersecurity disciplines.

Explore over 200 unique security challenges which you'll solve as a cybersecurity agent investigating criminal gangs.

Get access to an extensive field manual featuring video demos, top tips and essential background information to help with challenges.

Unlock a hidden interest, progress from novice to expert and demonstrate your skills to win scholarships.

scholarships.name: Augustana University - Journey Scholars Program & Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Who can apply for Journey Scholars?
Students from the U.S. who are admitted to Augustana University and identify on their application as being Black, Indigenous, Hispanic, Asian, or Person of Color.
Scholarships are awarded to all participants. For students with financial need, Augustana is committed to meeting the financial need of Journey Scholars as determined by the FAFSA.

Program features:
Access early campus orientation & programming.
Connect and regularly meet with an Augustana BIPOC per mentor.
Develop and implement a personalized academic plan.
scholarships.deadline: Prefered Deadline: 01/15 With Rolling Program Admission

scholarships.name: Profile in Courage Essay Contest
scholarships.criteria: The contest is open to US high school students in grades 9-12. Essays can be no more than 1,000 words but must be a minimum of 700 words. Citations and bibliography are not included in word count. Essays must describe an act of political courage by a U.S. elected official who served during or after 1917, the year John F. Kennedy was born. The official may have addressed an issue at the local, state, or national level. Must have a minimum of five sources. Must have nominating teacher who provides support and advice during the writing of their essay.

scholarships.name: South Dakota School of Mines Scholarships
scholarships.criteria: In order to be considered for incoming freshmen scholarships, prospective students must be accepted for admission to South Dakota Mines by the priority scholarship deadline of January 15 as well as have a 3.0 unweighted cumulative GPA from high school. The Office of Admissions will consider a student's highest composite score (either ACT or SAT) by test date. Please note ACT Superscores (calculated by ACT) will NOT be considered. After the deadline of January 15, no additional test scores or updated high school transcripts will be considered.

scholarships.name: CHS Scholarship
scholarships.criteria: Attention post-secondary bound students! We’re looking for the next generation of rural leaders, future producers and those passionate about the agricultural industry.Applicants must be a high school senior from the local CHS trade area, have a desire to work with the agricultural field and show enrollment in post-secondary education. Primary consideration will be given to applicants whose high school academic performance is high while demonstrating the qualities of leadership, passion for the industry, integrity and community involvement.

scholarships.name: Evie Kahnke Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.criteria: This scholarship has been established in memory of Evie Kahnke. Evie, the daughter of Chad and Hollie Kahnke, and sister to Emily and Charlie Kahnke, was an outstanding student-athlete and well rounded individual acitve in sports, FFA, 4H and her religion. She lost her three month battle to Acute Myeloid Luekemia at age 17, just days after her high school graduation. This scholarship is open to SD students who were active in extra curricular activities through all of his/her high school years and plan to pursue a career in teh ag industry.

scholarships.name: AES Engineering Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Students must submit an essay of between 500 and 1000 words in answer to the following question:
When you look back on your life in 30 years, what would it take for you to consider your life successful? What relationships or accomplishments will be important on this journey? Submit essay to scholarships@aesengineers.com

There is no application packet for this award. Please do not include your resume at this time.
Be sure to include your full name as well as the name of the school you are attending this year and your plans for next year.

scholarships.name: Sioux Valley Energy Scholarships
scholarships.criteria:
To be eligible you must:
Be a graduating high school senior or first-time attendee at an institution of higher education.
Plan to be a full-time student in an accredited college, vocational technical or accredited power line technical school this fall.
Be a son or daughter of a Sioux Valley Energy customer.
Have a 3.0 or higher cumulative GPA for a 4-year college and a minimum of a 2.5 or higher for a vocational/technical school.
Provide a written recommendation from a teacher, administrator or counselor.
One winner per family/per year.

scholarships.name: Fossi Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:

scholarships.name: Women In Science Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:

scholarships.criteria:

• Be sponsored by a current NTCA–The Rural Broadband
Association member (Alliance Communications)

scholarships.name: South Dakota Weed Fighters Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
The Association of SD County Weed and Pest Boards is accepting applications for post-secondary scholarships. To be eligible for Weed Fighter’s scholarship you must meet the following requirements:

Must be a citizen of the United States, and a South Dakota resident.
Must be a high school graduate, funding after you complete one semester in college
a post – secondary student with an agriculture production, precision farming, agronomy or entomology field of study in a South Dakota College, University or Technical School.

Have an identified disability (defined as someone who has, or considers themselves to have, a long-term or recurring issue that impacts one or more major life activity)
Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale or its equivalent

scholarships.amount: student will receive a $2,500 award for full-time study or a $1,250 award for half-time study

scholarships.name: Brandon Valley Area Chamber of Commerce Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Eligibility Requirements:
● Students must be a graduating Brandon Valley High School senior with a record of volunteerism in the community, in non-school sponsored activities, and/or participation in extracurricular school activities.
● Applicants must plan to attend an accredited post-high school college, university, vocational technical school, community college or junior college on a full-time basis.
● Application must be signed by both the parent and student in order to be considered and have a 3.0 GPA or above.

scholarships.name: ALLIANCE Communications Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
The Applicant’s household must be current customers of Alliance Communications, and the applicant must plan to be a full-time student in the fall. Completed application.
Two letters of recommendation. One letter must be from a teacher or school staff member.
A typed short essay (maximum 1 page in length) on one of these topics: Who has had the biggest impact on your life? What technological change has most affected you or your family? What is the best part of your community?
Transcript
ACT or SAT test scores

scholarships.criteria:

Black/African American,
Latinx,
Native North American,
Pacific Islander.
Enrolling as or enrolled as a full-time undergraduate student at a U.S. accredited educational institution.

$4,000 per student for a Utah university scholarship

scholarships.name: Study.com Scholarship for African Americans
scholarships.criteria:
"Must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent U.S. Resident.
Must be of African American Heritage.
Must be enrolled (or accepted) in an accredited college or university and planning on continuing the next year.
Graduating high school seniors who meet the above-mentioned criteria may apply.
Must have a minimum of 30 semester or 45 quarter hours still to be completed.
Must consent to provide a digital photograph of self and quote for display on Study.com if notified as the award winner by the selection committee."

scholarships.name: PB & J Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
The PB&J Scholarship is for students who have experienced personal challenges that may not have allowed them to perform well academically, but who still have the drive to succeed. Scholarship is open to senior high school students who plan on attending a 2 or 4 year college.

Examples of personal challenges include, but are not limited to:
medical issues
peer issues: bullying, change of school, minority status, etc.
family issues: divorce, death, lack of income, homelessness, foster care, abuse, etc.

scholarships.name: Grand Lodge A.F. & A.M. of South Dakota Scholarship
scholarships.criteria: Must be a South Dakota residents who plans to attend a public or private college, university or technical school. Preference will be given to students attending a school in South Dakota. Successful candidates will demonstrate financial need, scholastic capability, and have a family connection, either by blood or marriage, to a member of the Masonic fraternity, either living or deceased. Scholarships will be granted for one year, but may be applied for each year for a maximum of five years.

scholarships.name: The Generation Google Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Intend to be enrolled in or accepted as a full-time student in a Bachelors, Masters, or PhD program at an accredited university or college in the United States or Canada for the upcoming academic year

Be studying computer science, computer engineering, or a closely related technical field

Demonstrate a strong academic record

scholarships.name: Jan VandenBos Competitive Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Eligibility Requirements:

U19 player,
2) be a graduating senior with plans to continue your education (trade or certificate program, two-year college/technical
school or 4-year college or university)

scholarships.name: IVEY Essay Contest
scholarships.criteria:
The requirements for eligible student entries are:

You should presently be a senior in high school;
Or be transitioning from high school to a college or university;
Or be already enrolled as an undergraduate in a college or university inside the United States.
Employees and their immediate family members of Ivey Engineering are not eligible to participate.
Students with full academic scholarships are not eligible to enter.
Past winners are not eligible to participate in the contest.

scholarships.name: Dacotah Bank Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
ELIGIBILITY
TO BE ELIGIBLE FOR A DACOTAH BANK SCHOLARSHIP, YOU MUST MEET ALL OF THE FOLLOWING CRITERIA:

education institution in North Dakota, South Dakota or Minnesota

scholarships.name: Coca Cola Scholars Programs Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Applicants must be:Current high school (or home-schooled) seniors attending school in the United States (or select DoD schools)
U.S. Citizens, U.S. Nationals, U.S. Permanent Residents, Refugees, Asylees, Cuban-Haitian Entrants, or Humanitarian Parolees,
anticipating completion of high school diploma at the time of application,

carrying a minimum 3.00 GPA at the end of their junior year of high school.

scholarships.name: AG Bell College Scholarship Awards
scholarships.criteria: To be eligible, spoken communication must be the applicant's primary mode of communication and hearing loss must have been diagnosed before the applicant's fourth birthday. Hearing loss must be bilateral and in the moderate to profound range. Applicants must have an unaided Pure-Tone Average (PTA) of 60dB or greater in the better-hearing ear in the speech frequencies of 500, 1000 and 2000 Hz. For more information, or to apply, please visit the scholarship provider's website.

scholarships.name: Waste Management Four Corners Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Be pursuing a Diesel or Heavy Equipment Mechanic major.

Be a high school senior or graduate, or current college undergraduate.

Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year college or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year in Colorado, New Mexico, Utah or Arizona.

Have a minimum grade point average of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent).

WM employees and immediate family members of WM employees are ineligible.

scholarships.name: Men's College Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Available to any male, graduating high school senior who is enrolling in a four-year undergraduate college program commencing in fall 2023, scholarships will range from $500-$1,000 and will be issued in the form of a check for recipients to use as desired.

The scholarship is designed to identify and reward outstanding high school seniors who have demonstrated an ability to excel in the fields of academics, extra-curricular school activities and community involvement.

scholarships.name: Citi Youth Leadership Award Scholarship
scholarships.criteria: Students need to be a senior at a Sioux Empire high school during the 2020-2021 academic year. Students need to have contributed at least 100 hours of service within the past 12 months. Eligible service may include: service with community/religious organizations; service through school/community based service-learning projects or individual efforts to help others and/or improve the community. This service cannot include fundraising, lobbying, or paid/stipend service.

scholarships.name: Trane Technnician of the Future
scholarships.criteria:
Be a current high school senior, high school graduate or current college undergraduate in an eligible region in the US and Canada.

Be pursuing an HVAC (Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning) degree or certification or building automation technology degree or certification.

plan to enroll in part-time or fulltime undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical/trade school for the upcoming academic term.

scholarships.name: The Weber Shandwick Scholarship
scholarships.criteria: The Weber Shandwick Scholarship is currently accepting applications from high school seniors, and anyone currently enrolled in an undergraduate college or university. The Weber Shandwick Scholarship is not merit based, so you don't need to submit any grades or test scores. All you have to do is write one 400-600 word essay. Your essay should address the following question: "How can emerging technology contribute to a more fair, accessible, or inclusive world?"

scholarships.name: Marv Veldkamp Softball Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
REQUIREMENTS:
1. Brandon Valley High School Senior – graduating 2021
2. Played BVHS Softball all four years of high school
3. Minimum of two years on the Varsity Team
4. Minimum Cumulative GPA of 3.0 – end Semester one 2020-2021
5. Applicant/winner does not have to play college softball
6. Essay – in 500 words, or less, write an essay on “The Life Lessons I Learned from the Game of Softball”
Return application with essay to Mr. Randy Marso (Athletic Director)

scholarships.name: Unigo: Shout It Out Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Applicants must:

This award is for U.S. students.| Must be a legal U.S. resident.| Must be a resident of one of the 50 United States or the District of Columbia.| Must be 14 years of age or older at time of application.

Submit an online written response to the question:

"If you could say one thing to the entire world at once, what would it be and why?" (250 words or less)

The Shout It Out Scholarship winner will be notified by email or phone on or around

scholarships.name: The Banner Student Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
Eligibility Requirements:
1. Must be a senior student planning to attend a 4-year college or university the fall following graduation.
2. Applicant has shown academic achievement by earning a GPA of 3.5 or higher.
3. Applicant has 4 years of dedicated participation in a music ensemble (band, chorus, orchestra).
4. Applicant has 4 years of dedicated participation in athletics.
Applications can be submitted to Bill Freking, BVHS Athletic Director.

scholarships.name: Ramia Boersma Scholarship
scholarships.criteria: Scholarships are awarded to outstanding students who are planning on entering the teaching profession. Criteria for the application requires that the student must: 1. Be the dughter/son or grandaughter/grandson of an active member or an SDEA-Retired member. 2. Be in the top quarter of his/her class as of January of graduating year. 3. Be a student in a SD public education institution. 4. Be accepted and/or enrolled in a SD college or university.

scholarships.name: Huge - Nebraska Wesleyan University Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:
To qualify, a student must:

Submit the Nebraska Wesleyan University application for admission.

scholarships.name: Empower Manufacturing Scholarship for 11th Graders by Powerblanket
scholarships.criteria:

scholarships.name: Annual Louise W Pilgrim (LWP) Scholarship

scholarships.name: AGC of SD HHU Chapter Scholarships
scholarships.criteria: The AGC of SD Highway-Heavy-Utilities Chapter is committed to providing scholarships for students pursuing a career in a construction-related education program at a college/university or technical institute. scholarships.name: Chad Garrow Scholarship

Essay Requirements

scholarships.name: Elks Legacy Award

scholarships.criteria: BY RECCOMENDATION ONLY. Students will be asked to discuss how their chosen Patriot contributed to the founding of the nation. scholarships.name: South Dakota Farmers Union Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.criteria:

Step 1: Understand the Different Types of Financial Aid
Before embarking on the financial aid journey, it's crucial to understand the different types of options available and their implications.

Scholarships: Scholarships are merit-based awards that do not require repayment. They are typically awarded based on academic achievement, extracurricular involvement, or other factors such as leadership potential or artistic talent.
Grants: Grants are need-based financial aid that does not require repayment. They are typically awarded to students from low-income families or those with demonstrated financial need.

Loans: Loans are funds that must be repaid, with interest, over time. They are available to students regardless of financial need and can be a valuable option for covering the remaining costs of education after scholarships and grants have been applied.
Step 2: Start Early and Plan Ahead

The search for financial aid should begin early, ideally in the high school years. Many scholarships and grants have application deadlines as early as the fall of the senior year, so starting early gives students a better chance of securing funding.
Step 3: Identify Potential Sources of Financial Aid
There are numerous sources of financial aid, including:
Federal government: The U.S. Department of Education offers a variety of grants and loans, including the Pell Grant and the Direct Subsidized Loan.
State governments: Many states offer their own financial aid programs, often based on financial need and residency.
Colleges and universities: Most colleges and universities offer their own scholarships and grants, often based on academic achievement or specific areas of study.
Private organizations: Numerous private foundations, corporations, and community groups offer scholarships and grants based on various criteria.
Step 4: Complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA)

The FAFSA is the gateway to federal and state financial aid. It is required for all students seeking financial aid, regardless of their family's income. The FAFSA is typically completed in the spring of the junior year of high school.
Step 5: Research and Apply for Scholarships

Most scholarship applications require essays, letters of recommendation, and transcripts. It's important to start preparing these materials well in advance, ensuring they are well-written, error-free, and showcase the student's strengths and achievements.
Step 7: Meet Deadlines and Stay Organized

Financial aid deadlines can vary widely, so it's crucial to keep track of important dates and submit applications promptly. Staying organized and maintaining a detailed record of applications can help avoid missed opportunities.

Work-study programs allow students to earn money to help pay for college expenses while attending school part-time. These programs can be a valuable source of funding, especially for students who want to contribute to their education costs.
Step 10: Seek Guidance from Financial Aid Professionals

Financial aid professionals at colleges, high schools, and community organizations can provide valuable guidance and assistance throughout the financial aid process. They can help students understand their options, complete applications, and make informed decisions about funding their college education.

Funding a college education can be a daunting task, but with careful planning, research, and a proactive approach, families can navigate the financial aid landscape and find the resources they need to make college dreams a reality. Remember, the key is to start early, explore all available options, and seek guidance when needed.
